title: What the draft market pays for
summary: Spearman rank correlation between each Combine number and draft slot (UDFA = pick 262), signed so that positive means 'better number, earlier pick'. Strongest links: NGS final for DB (ρ=0.76, n=122); NGS final for WR (ρ=0.75, n=106); NGS final for DL (ρ=0.74, n=118); NGS final for OL (ρ=0.74, n=121); NGS final for TE (ρ=0.72, n=42).
method: Spearman ρ per position group; p-values two-sided; n = players with both values.

title: What actually correlates with NFL production
summary: Rank correlation between pre-draft numbers and a per-position production rate (WR/TE yards per route, OL pressure rate allowed, DL pressure rate, DB solo tackles per 100 snaps), signed so positive = better number, better outcome. Draft slot is the strongest signal of opportunity everywhere (ρ with snaps per season from -0.85 to -0.70), but of production only in some groups. Statistically clear links (p<0.05): 3-cone→Pressure rate for DL (ρ=0.61, n=27); 40-yard→Pressure rate for DL (ρ=0.50, n=54); Shuttle→Pressure rate for DL (ρ=0.50, n=26); NGS final→Pressure rate for DL (ρ=0.49, n=69); 10-yd split→Pressure rate for DL (ρ=0.48, n=54); Tracked top speed→Pressure rate for DL (ρ=0.47, n=53); Draft pick (log)→Yards per route run for WR (ρ=0.43, n=58); Broad jump→Pressure rate for DL (ρ=0.41, n=61).
method: Spearman ρ; players above a minimum sample (WR 150 routes, OL 150 pass blocks, DL 100 rush snaps, DB 150 plays). Production is aggregated over all regular seasons played.

title: The sensor sees the finish, not the start
summary: Elapsed time from the first tracked frame to 40 yards correlates r=0.91 with the official laser time (n=381), but is 0.32 s longer on average (sd 0.13): the clip includes the stance and the first rock before the timer starts on forward movement, and that pre-start window varies by player. The 10-yard split agrees far worse (r=0.47, n=418) because it sits entirely inside that noisy start, while tracked top speed alone predicts the official 40 at |r|=0.98 (n=418). Use the tracking for the shape of the run (where top speed is reached, how it decays), never as a replacement for the stopwatch, and treat the first 10 yards with suspicion.
method: Best attempt per player; 40-yard elapsed from x displacement; Pearson r.

title: Drills are not comparable across Combine years without adjustment
summary: Median of each drill's key metric by Combine year. The spread is expressed in within-drill standard deviations; anything above ~0.5 means a player's percentile depends more on which year he attended than on how he moved. Largest gaps: Slant (2.9 sd); Wheel (2.0 sd); Backpedal & 45° Transition (1.9 sd); Run and Club (1.5 sd); Corner Route (1.5 sd); Wave Drill & Lateral Reaction (1.4 sd). Every cross-class comparison in the analysis is therefore made on year-standardized values.
method: Median key metric per draft year; spread = (max − min) / pooled sd.

title: Most position drills are single-attempt, and the repeats barely agree
summary: Only 9 drills have at least 15 players with two attempts. Where they exist, the rank correlation between attempt 1 and attempt 2 of the key metric ranges from -0.03 to 0.98. The 40 and the timed agility drills repeat well; reaction-based position drills do not, so any single-attempt drill metric carries large measurement error and must be shrunk toward the position mean before it is used to rank prospects.
method: Spearman ρ between attempt 1 and attempt 2 of the key metric; drills with ≥15 such players.

title: Edge/DL: does the pass-rush drill get-off show up in games?
summary: Among 69 DL/EDGE with 100+ pass-rush snaps, peak acceleration in the Combine pass-rush drill correlates ρ=-0.31 (p=0.011, n=69) with in-game get-off time (negative = quicker off the ball). The heatmap compares every drill-derived number against get-off, pressure rate and opportunity; the official 10-yard split is the benchmark to beat.
method: Spearman ρ; DL/EDGE with ≥100 regular-season pass-rush snaps; drill values are the best attempt.

rows: Pass rush drill: time to 5 yd/s

title: WR: route-drill break mechanics vs in-game separation
summary: For wide receivers with 150+ routes (n≈52 per drill), rank correlations between break metrics from each route drill and NFL separation / yards per route. Largest: Slant burst out of break→Yards per route ρ=0.38 (p=0.08); Go Route decel into break→Avg separation ρ=0.31 (p=0.28); Go Route burst out of break→Yards per route ρ=0.29 (p=0.31); Slant break angle→Yards per route ρ=-0.27 (p=0.22); Go Route decel into break→Yards per route ρ=0.24 (p=0.41); Go Route top speed→Avg separation ρ=0.24 (p=0.09); Slant speed through break→Yards per route ρ=0.23 (p=0.30); Go Route burst out of break→Avg separation ρ=0.22 (p=0.45). With one attempt per drill and ~60 players, few of these clear p<0.05; this is the baseline the translation analysis has to improve on.
method: Spearman ρ on best attempt per drill; separation is route-weighted across seasons.

title: Expected vs actual: who beat his draft slot
summary: Ridge regression (5-fold CV) of two outcomes on draft slot alone, then adding Combine numbers, then adding tracking features. Opportunity (snaps per season) is well explained by the pick (CV R² 0.46–0.62); Combine numbers add between -0.20 and +0.14 R², and tracking features add -0.05 to +0.06. The residual of the pick + Combine model is the player's 'value over draft slot': positive means more snaps or better production than a prospect with his pick and his numbers normally gets. The tables below list the largest residuals per group; the same number is shown on every player card.
method: RidgeCV on standardized features, median-imputed; CV R² = 1 − SSE/SST on out-of-fold predictions. Production targets use the same thresholds as the correlation table.

title: Largest over- and under-performers vs expectation
summary: Top five and bottom five residuals per group for opportunity (snaps per season) and for production. Positive z = did more than the model expected from pick and Combine numbers. Early picks dominate the 'under' lists by construction: the model expects a lot of them.
method: Residual z-score within group from the pick + Combine ridge model.
